title: 1967 Nicosia Britannia disaster
summary: A Bristol Britannia of Swiss airline Globe Air operating a charter flight from Bangkok to Basel was diverted to Nicosia International Airport in Cyprus due to bad weather at Cairo on April 20, 1967. The aircraft made three landing attempts in violent thunderstorm conditions. During the third approach to Runway 32, the aircraft flew into a hill near the village of Lakatamia and burst into flames, killing 126 of the 130 people aboard. Investigation noted that both pilots had exceeded their authorized duty time by three hours at the time of the accident.
probable_cause: Controlled flight into terrain during approach in severe thunderstorm conditions, with contributing factors of crew fatigue from exceeded duty time limits and deteriorated crew performance during multiple approach attempts in severe weather.

title: Stockport air disaster
summary: On 4 June 1967, a Canadair C-4 Argonaut passenger aircraft owned by British Midland Airways operating as British Midland Flight 542 crashed near the centre of Stockport, Cheshire, England. Of the 84 people on board, 72 were killed. It is the fourth-worst accident in British aviation history, and happened just a day after the 1967 Air Ferry DC-4 accident. title: Aeroflot 2230
summary: Aeroflot Flight 2230 was a Soviet domestic passenger flight from Yekaterinburg (then Sverdlovsk) to Tashkent.  On 16 November 1967, the Ilyushin Il-18 aircraft serving the flight crashed after takeoff, killing all 107 people aboard (including twelve children). At the time, it was the deadliest aviation accident in the Russian SFSR and the worst accident involving the Il-18.
